introduction: Legal Services of New Jersey offers free civil legal help to eligible low-income residents. Use its legal-help application to request screening and explain any urgent court date.

sections.who: LSNJ screens the financial circumstances and legal issue. A request may lead to advice, another service or a referral; it does not automatically establish lawyer representation.
sections.get: The organization provides legal assistance and self-help information. Keep the distinction between a general guide and advice about your own court papers clear.
sections.docs:
• Court documents, notices or benefit decisions.
  • The next response deadline or hearing date.
  • A short timeline of events.
  • Household and income details requested at intake.
sections.apply:
1. Open the provider application

    Follow Apply for Legal Help on LSNJ’s website to the hotline intake.

  2. Describe the issue and urgency

    Identify the notice, court or agency involved and the upcoming date. Ask which supporting documents the screener needs.

  3. Confirm the service offered

    Ask whether the case has been accepted, who will contact you and what you need to do while waiting.
sections.after: Keep application and response records. If the organization cannot take the matter, ask for a referral and continue tracking the actual court or agency deadline.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using LSNJ current legal-help application and purpose. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Is the application the same as hiring a lawyer?
No. The provider must confirm the assistance it agrees to provide.
Can I use the self-help site before intake?
Yes. LSNJ links self-help resources alongside its legal-help application.
What should I emphasize about an eviction?
Identify the notice, filed court papers and hearing or response date.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
